memoryText: Fear not, I am the first and the last, and the living one. I died, and behold I am alive forevermore, and I have the keys of Death and Hades.
readingInstruction: No new reading today. Read Revelation 1:17-18 slowly, several times, and try to say it from memory. Then read the meditation and the week in review, and choose one of the three questions to write about, pray over, or share with someone.
memoryVerseMeditation:
John, the beloved disciple who once leaned on Jesus’ chest at supper, falls at his feet as though dead when he sees the risen Christ in glory. Even for a friend, the glory of the Lord is overwhelming. And then Jesus lays his right hand on him and speaks the most common command in the Bible: “Fear not.”

The reason is who Jesus is: the first and the last, the living one. He has always been and will always be. And his credentials are astonishing: “I died, and behold I am alive forevermore.” He has gone through the one door that no one else returned from. He holds the keys of Death and Hades.

If he holds the keys, then death is not a locked door he cannot open; the grave has an owner, and he is your Savior. When fear comes today, put your hand in his right hand, the one he laid on John, and hear him say again, “Fear not.”
weekInReview: This week you began the book of Revelation. Chapter 1 unveiled the risen Christ: the faithful witness, the firstborn of the dead, and the ruler of kings, the Alpha and Omega, the Son of Man in glory with a sword in his mouth and the keys of Death and Hades in his hand, walking among his churches. Chapter 2 gave his letters to Ephesus (love grown cold), Smyrna (faithful in suffering), Pergamum (compromise with the world), and Thyatira (tolerating false teaching), each with a promise to the one who conquers: the tree of life, the crown of life, the hidden manna and white stone, and the morning star.
reflectionQuestions: John saw Jesus in glory and fell as though dead, yet Jesus touched him and said, “Fear not.” What fear do you most need Jesus to speak that word over right now?

Ephesus had sound doctrine but had lost its first love. Honestly, how would you describe your love for Christ and for his people right now, and what is one step toward returning to the works you did at first?
Jesus says to the conqueror at Smyrna that he will receive the crown of life. How does the promise that Christ himself died and came to life help you face suffering or fear of death?
prayerPrompts: Thank Jesus that he is the first and the last, the living one.
Thank him that he holds the keys of death and Hades.
